role: Shared localized-literal extractor imported by check_localization_resolution.sh and check_localization_orphans.sh, so both gates agree on which Swift literals are catalogue lookups and what key each resolves to.
state: SPECIFIER: regex for format specifiers (%@ %lld %ld %d %u %.Nf %f %s, optional positional N$)
SWIFTUI_IMPLICIT / SWIFTUI_MODIFIERS: call names that take a LocalizedStringKey
CALL: regex matching the start of every localizing call
toplevel: Module docstring, `import re`, and the constants above. No code runs on import.

units.does: Reads a Swift triple-quoted literal starting at i: body from after the newline following the opening delimiter, closing-line indentation stripped from each line, backslash-newline joins removed, then scanned as a one-line literal (interpolations become INTERP). Returns (body, index after the closing delimiter); an unterminated literal returns ("", len(text)).

Returns (body, index after closing quote) for the literal opening at text[i]; delegates triple quotes to scan_multiline_literal. Walks escapes, replaces each \( ... ) interpolation (tracking nested parens and nested literals) with INTERP, keeps other escapes verbatim. An unterminated literal returns what was read and len(text).

branches.effect: skipped to its matching paren, INTERP appended

units.does: Turns Swift escapes (\u{...}, \", \n, \t, \', \\) in a literal body into the characters they stand for.
Both keys one literal can resolve to: with literal % doubled (as Xcode writes keys) and without (hand-authored format templates); interpolations become %@ in both.
Compiles an anchored regex matching catalogue keys equal to the candidate with each %@ accepting any SPECIFIER spelling.

True when the literal at start is not a LocalizedStringKey: it follows `[` (a subscript key) or `??` (the Text(String) overload of nil-coalescing, which does not localize), judged by the nearest non-whitespace characters before it.

Literals at paren depth 1 in the first argument of a call whose opening paren is already consumed, stopping at the first top-level comma or the closing paren; skips literals skip_literal_at rejects and literals nested in inner calls.

branches.cond: top-level literal that is a key

units.does: Yields (line, body) for every literal a localizing call in the text looks up: String/AttributedString(localized:), LocalizedStringKey(, NSLocalizedString(, SwiftUI Text/Button/Label/Toggle/TextField/Picker/Section, and the .navigationTitle/.alert/.confirmationDialog/.accessibilityLabel/.accessibilityHint/.value modifiers. A literal right after the paren is taken directly; otherwise the first argument is scanned. Text(verbatim:) is skipped.
